**Approach.** Model the first resonance as the even quasi-bound state of the well. Take the well centred on x=0 with edges at ±2.5 nm, and use an outgoing-wave condition in the outer contact. Propagating through a barrier of width b=2 nm gives a log-derivative match at the well edge.

**Setup.** Let ħ²/2m = 0.568653 eV nm² (from 0.0380998/0.067). Define
- k² = E/0.568653 (well),
- κ² = (V0−E)/0.568653 (barrier),
- K0² = κ²+k² = V0/0.568653 = 0.527633 nm⁻².

**Matching condition.** The even-state condition in the well is k tan(kL/2) = F, with L = 5 nm. The barrier-side function is

F = κ[(κ²+k²) sinh(2κb)cosh(2κb) − i kκ] / [κ²cosh²(2κb) + k² sinh²(2κb)].

The imaginary part of F is the resonance width. I dropped it and used the real part, which is the standard approximation for locating the peak. Because these barriers are thin, the resonance is broad, so this introduces some uncertainty in the last digit.

Real-part condition:

k tan(kL/2) = κ K0² sinh(2κb)cosh(2κb) / [κ²cosh²(2κb) + k² sinh²(2κb)]

**Numerical root.** Evaluating f(E) = LHS − RHS:

| E (eV) | LHS | RHS | f |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.080 | 0.511 | 0.570 | −0.059 |
| 0.085 | 0.560 | 0.565 | −0.004 |
| 0.100 | 0.728 | 0.549 | +0.179 |

Linear interpolation between 0.080 and 0.085 gives a root at E ≈ 0.0854 eV.

For comparison, an infinite well of width 5 nm would have its ground state at 0.2245 eV, so the finite barriers pull the first resonance well below that value. The estimate is consistent with this.
